question.text: What role does the Financial Intelligence Unit - India (FIU-IND) play in the AML framework?

answer.text: It serves as the central national agency for receiving, processing, analyzing, and disseminating information related to suspect financial transactions
It directly investigates and prosecutes money laundering cases in courts
It issues licenses to banks and financial institutions for operating in India
It sets monetary policy and controls inflation in the Indian economy

explanation.text: The Logic: FIU-IND is the central national agency for collecting, processing, analyzing and disseminating information on suspect financial transactions. It maintains a central repository of such reports and coordinates with relevant agencies, acting as the country's financial-intelligence hub. The Trap: Investigation and prosecution of money-laundering cases is the role of the Directorate of Enforcement, not FIU-IND. Licensing of banks and setting monetary policy are functions of other regulators. Note: Treat FIU-IND as the analysis-and-dissemination layer and the Directorate of Enforcement as the investigation layer when mapping AML responsibilities.
